This is just a short post regarding Brexit. Setting aside economic, political
and social considerations, there is another consequence: there is now one fewer
country in the EU.

We will miss you, UK. We wish you the best.

<div role="note" aria-label="Note" class="callout-note" markdown="1">
**Historical example:** The mapping examples use **cartography**, which is now
in maintenance mode. Its maintainers recommend [**mapsf**](https://riatelab.github.io/mapsf/)
for new work. The original code and outputs are preserved and have not been
revalidated against current package versions.
</div>

```{r}
#| label: 20200602_imgpost
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-height: !expr 540/90
#| fig-width: !expr 810/90
#| fig-format: ragg_png
#| fig-dpi: 90
#| fig-cap: ""
#| fig-alt: "Map of Europe overlaid with the European Union flag. The United Kingdom is left white to illustrate Brexit."
library(cartography)
library(sf)
library(giscoR)


# EU
eu <- giscoR::gisco_countrycode %>% filter(eu)

# Download maps
NUTS1 <- gisco_get_nuts(epsg = 3035, country = eu$ISO3_CODE, nuts_level = 1)


UK <- gisco_get_countries(country = "GBR", epsg = 3035)

noplot <- c("FRY", "ES7", "PT2", "PT3")
NUTS1_Clean <- NUTS1 %>%
  subset(!NUTS_ID %in% noplot) %>%
  group_by(CNTR_CODE) %>%
  summarise(a = dplyr::n())

# Flag image
url <- "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b7/Flag_of_Europe.svg/800px-Flag_of_Europe.svg.png"

# Mask UK
flagcut <- getPngLayer(
  NUTS1_Clean,
  url
)
# Full extent
flag <- getPngLayer(NUTS1_Clean,
  url,
  mask = FALSE
)


par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
tilesLayer(flag, alpha = 150)
tilesLayer(flagcut, bgalpha = 0, add = T)
plot(st_geometry(UK),
  col = "white",
  border = NA,
  add = TRUE
)
```
